category: cross-border payment intermediary (Iran; pays foreign subscriptions on the customer's behalf)

free_tier.stated: not applicable: a payment service, not a retrieval service.
free_tier.notes: The article is dated 2023-11-29; the firm's current fee schedule was not read.

interface_detail: A web service with a subscription-purchase page (cafearz.com/buy-subscription) and a blog; the order form itself was not opened.
chaining: For a client in Iran this is the substitute for a card: the firm takes Toman and settles the foreign charge, so a debrid subscription priced in euro becomes payable without a foreign card and without a reseller's markup on the account itself.

limits.value: every purchase is an order a human or a compliance step must accept before the foreign charge is made

limits_note: The firm's own article frames the problem as structural: buying a foreign subscription from Iran 'has many challenges' and requires a company of this kind.
binding_note: There is no byte quota to bind; what binds is the intermediary's willingness and capacity to settle the charge, which is an approval rather than a counter.

identity_cost.detail: A customer account with the firm. Iranian exchange businesses normally verify identity, but the KYC fields were not read here, so the tier is recorded as email and flagged as probably higher.

reliability_note: A user's subscription depends on the intermediary's own foreign accounts staying open; when an intermediary loses its settlement path, every subscription it paid for lapses at once.
confidence_note: The article's statement of the problem and the existence of the subscription service were read. Fees, settlement time and the identity fields are unread, so the record documents the rail's existence rather than its price.

evidence.proved: 'خرید اشتراک از سایت های خارجی در ایران چالش زیاد دارد و ما برای پرداخت هزینه آن باید از شرکت‌هایی نظیر کافه ارز کمک بگیریم', plus the link to its subscription-purchase service

notes: No fee was read, so no cost claim is made.
